body.p: This listing of claims will replace all prior versions and listings of claims in the application.

br.br:
Claim 1 (Currently Amended): A system comprising:
an insertable cardiac monitor (ICM) comprising:
a housing configured for subcutaneous implantation within a patient, the housing having a length extending from a proximal end of the housing to a distal end of the housing, a width, and a depth, wherein the length is greater than the width and the width is greater than the depth, and
wherein the length is within a range from 40 millimeters (mm) to 60 mm;
a heart sound sensor, wherein the ICM is configured to sense heart sounds of the patient via the heart sound sensor; and
a plurality of electrodes on the housing, wherein the ICM is configured to sense an electrocardiogram (ECG) of the patient via the plurality of electrodes;
a remote computing device; and
processing circuitry of at least one of the insertable cardiac monitor or the remote computing device, the processing circuitry configured to:
periodically determine a respective value for each of a plurality of physiological parameters based on one or more of the heart sounds or the ECG, wherein at least a first physiological parameter of the plurality of physiological parameters is determined based on the heart sounds and at least a second physiological parameter of the plurality of physiological parameters is determined based on the ECG;
output trends of the periodically determined values of the physiological parameters at the remote computing device; and
determine whether to present an indication of a cardiac heart failure event based on an analysis of the trends of the periodically determined values of the physiological parameters.
Claim 2 (Canceled).
Claim 3 (Currently Amended): The system of claim 1, wherein the indication of the cardiac heart failure event comprises an indication of a risk of the cardiac heart failure event.
Claim 4 (Currently Amended): The system of claim 1, wherein to determine whether to present the indication of the cardiac heart failure event based on an analysis of the trends of the periodically determined periodically determined values of the physiological parameters, the processing circuitry is configured to apply respective weights to each of the plurality of physiological parameters.
Claim 5 (Original): The system of claim 1, wherein the plurality of physiological parameters comprise a measurement of an SI heart sound.
Claim 6 (Original): The system of claim 1, wherein the plurality of physiological parameters comprise a measurement of an S3 heart sound.
Claim 7 (Original): The system of claim 1, wherein the plurality of physiological parameters comprise one or more of: a morphological measurement of an S I and/or S2 heart sound, or a presence/frequency of an S3 and/or S4 heart sound.
Claim 8 (Original): The system of claim 1, wherein the plurality of physiological parameters comprise a morphological measurement of an S1 heart sound.
Claim 9 (Original): The system of claim 1, wherein the plurality of physiological parameters comprise a presence/frequency of an S3 heart sound.
Claim 10 (Original): The system of claim 1, wherein the ICM comprises a patient activity sensor configured to sense activity/posture of the patient, and the processing circuitry is configured to periodically determine values of at least one physiological parameter of the plurality of physiological parameters based on the sensed activity/posture.
Claim 11 (Currently Amended): The system of claim 1, wherein the ICM comprises one or more accelerometers configured to generate, and the processing circuitry is configured to periodically determine values of at least one physiological parameter of the plurality of physiological parameters based on a signal from the one or more accelerometers.
Claim 12 (Currently Amended): The system of claim 1, wherein the processing circuitry is configured to determine whether a change of at least one of the physiological parameters in a period is significantly greater than a variation in the physiological parameter during prior periods, and determine whether to present the indication of the cardiac heart failure event based on the determination of whether the change in the period is significantly greater than the variation during the prior periods.
Claim 13 (Currently Amended): The system of claim 1, wherein the processing circuitry is configured to determine whether to present the indication of the cardiac heart failure event based on a comparison of a physiological parameter value for a current period to a threshold determined based on physiological parameter values for previous periods.
Claim 14 (Original): The system of claim 1, wherein the plurality of physiological parameters comprises at least one of a heart rate variability parameter or a night heart rate parameter.
Claim 15 (Original): The system of claim 1, wherein the housing defines an elongated rectangular prism comprising a rounded distal end and a rounded proximal end.
Claim 16 (Original): The system of claim 1, wherein the plurality of electrodes comprises a first electrode that is substantially flat and a second electrode that comprises a three-dimensional, curved configuration.
Claim 17 (Original): The system of claim 1, wherein a volume of the ICM is less than 1.5 cubic centimeters.

periodically determine a respective value for each of a plurality of physiological parameters based on one or more of heart sounds or an electrocardiogram (ECG) sensed by an insertable cardiac monitor (ICM), wherein at least a first physiological parameter of the plurality of physiological parameters is determined based on the heart sounds and at least a second physiological parameter of the plurality of physiological parameters is determined based on the ECG, wherein the ICM comprises:
a housing configured for subcutaneous implantation within a patient, the housing having a length extending from a proximal end of the housing to a distal end of the housing, a width, and a depth, wherein the length is greater than the width and the width is greater than the depth, and
wherein the length is within a range from 40 millimeters (mm) to 60 mm;
a heart sound sensor, wherein the ICM is configured to sense the heart sounds via the heart sound sensor; and
a plurality of electrodes on the housing, wherein the ICM is configured to sense the ECG via the plurality of electrodes;
output trends of the periodically determined values of the physiological parameters at a remote computing device; and
determine whether to present an indication of a cardiac heart failure event based on an analysis of the trends of the periodically determined values of the physiological parameters.
Claim 19 (Canceled).
Claim 20 (Currently Amended): The non-transitory computer-readable storage medium of claim 18, wherein the indication of the cardiac heart failure event comprises an indication of a risk of the cardiac heart failure event.
Claim 21 (Original): The non-transitory computer-readable storage medium of claim 18, wherein the plurality of physiological parameters comprise a measurement of an S1 heart sound.
Claim 22 (Original): The non-transitory computer-readable storage medium of claim 18, wherein the plurality of physiological parameters comprise a measurement of an S3 heart sound.
Claim 23 (Original): The non-transitory computer-readable storage medium of claim 18, wherein the plurality of physiological parameters comprise one or more of: a morphological measurement of an S1 and/or S2 heart sound, or a presence/frequency of an S3 and/or S4 heart sound.

Claim 27 (Currently Amended): An insertable cardiac monitor (ICM) comprising:
a housing configured for subcutaneous implantation within a patient, the housing having a length extending from a proximal end of the housing to a distal end of the housing, a width, and a depth, wherein the length is greater than the width and the width is greater than the depth, wherein the length is within a range from 40 millimeters (mm) to 60 mm;
a heart sound sensor, wherein the ICM is configured to sense heart sounds of the patient via the heart sounds sensor;
a plurality of electrodes on the housing, wherein the ICM is configured to sense an electrocardiogram (ECG) of the patient via the plurality of electrodes; and
communication circuitry within the housing; and
processing circuitry within the housing, the processing circuitry configured to:
cause the communication circuitry to establish one or more telemetry communication sessions with a remote computing device; and
cause the communication circuitry to, during the one or more telemetry communication sessions, communicate values of a plurality of physiological parameters periodically determined based at least in part on one or more of the heart sounds or the ECG to the remote computing device, wherein at least a first physiological parameter of the plurality of physiological parameters is determined based on the heart sounds and at least a second physiological parameter of the plurality of physiological parameters is determined based on the ECG, wherein the remote computing device that is configured to output trends of the periodically determined values of the physiological parameters and is further configured to determine whether to present an indication of a cardiac heart failure event based on an analysis of the trends of the periodically determined values of the physiological parameters.
Claim 28 (Original): The insertable cardiac monitor (ICM) of claim 27, wherein the plurality of physiological parameters comprise at least one of a measurement of an S1 heart sound or a measurement of an S3 heart sound.

Claim 30 (Original): The system of claim 29, wherein the plurality of physiological parameters comprise at least one of a measurement of an Si heart sound or a measurement of an S3 heart sound.
Claim 31 (New): The system of claim 1, wherein the ICM is configured to sense the ECG via a proximal electrode of the plurality of electrodes at the proximal end and a distal electrode of the plurality of electrodes at the distal end.
